subject: SOC 2 Type II & GDPR: scope, interim attestation (bridge) and KMS evidence
messages:
From: Sofia Clarke <sofia.clarke@midlandbank.co.uk>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Procurement <legal@midlandbank.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial compliance ask — SOC 2 Type II, DPA and interim coverage

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. As part of our procurement risk review I need to gather a few items to move Redwood through Midland Bank's security sign-off. Can you confirm the following: 

1) Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report that covers the period through at least 2025-06 (or an interim attestation covering the gap to a newer report)? If the current report ends before our contract start date we will need an interim attestation or bridge statement that clarifies coverage and what controls remain in place while the next audit is completed.

2) Where are customer production workloads hosted for EU/UK customers? We need clarity on the processing boundary vs control plane (region and responsible sub-processors).

3) For cryptographic key management, can you confirm whether keys are customer-dedicated or Redwood-managed, the KMS vendor, and if HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise customers? We also need a short description of evidence you can provide (KMS config snapshots, logs showing key usage, or a procedural control).

4) Do you rely on SCCs or other transfer mechanisms for cross-border processing, and can you provide the relevant DPA language or a draft DPA we can circulate with our legal team?

If possible, please attach the SOC 2 report (redacted where needed), a draft DPA, and a short KMS configuration summary. We are timing procurement to finish by the end of March so a 1-week turnaround would be ideal.

Thanks,

Sofia Clarke
Head of Vendor Risk — Midland Bank
sofia.clarke@midlandbank.co.uk
+44 20 7946 0999
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sofia Clarke <sofia.clarke@midlandbank.co.uk>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial compliance ask — SOC 2 Type II, DPA and interim coverage

Hi Sofia,

Appreciate the clear list — we can absolutely support this. Attached are: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06.pdf (redacted), a draft DPA we typically use for UK/EU customers (DPA_Draft_MidlandBank.docx) and a short KMS_Configuration_Summary.txt with the high-level details below.

Quick answers up front: 
- SOC 2: Our most recent Type II report covers 2024-01 through 2025-06. We are currently under audit for a 2025-07 through 2026-06 window; the auditor expects final deliverables in Q3 2026. We can provide an interim attestation (we call it an "interim coverage letter") signed by our compliance director that states which control areas remain in effect while the audit completes. That letter can be scoped to your required contract start date (please confirm the date you need covered).

- Hosting/processing boundary: For UK customers we offer a UK processing option hosted in AWS eu-west-2 (London) for customer production workloads; control plane metadata and telemetry may be routed via our control plane in eu-west-1 (Ireland) unless the customer elects our Private deployment. The attached DPA highlights subprocessors and regions. If you need a fully isolated control plane (Private), we can discuss a dedicated VPC deployment and an on-premise control-plane alternative.

- KMS: We offer both Redwood-managed KMS and a customer-supplied key option. The managed option uses AWS KMS with multi-region keys; enterprise customers can request HSM-backed keys (AWS CloudHSM) and support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flows. The attachment includes the minimal artifacts we can share: key policy snippets, recent KMS audit log examples (redacted), and a description of key rotation controls. For full BYOK/HSM deployments we run a short onboarding checklist with our security engineering team.

- Cross-border transfers: Our standard mechanism is EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) embedded in the DPA and, where applicable, an internal transfer impact assessment. We can produce a short summary confirming no automated transfers outside the UK/EU for data tagged as restricted; non-sensitive telemetry may traverse regions for routing/failover.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the contract effective date you need covered so we can scope the interim coverage letter.
2) Let us know if Midland requires the control plane to be UK-only or if eu-west-1 control plane routing is acceptable.
3) If BYOK/HSM is required, we will loop in Security Engineering to scope provisioning and an estimated 3-6 week lead time.

I'll follow up with Rishi on the KMS evidence you requested and copy Grace (our head of customer success) to coordinate timelines.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06.pdf (redacted), DPA_Draft_MidlandBank.docx, KMS_Configuration_Summary.txt
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Sofia Clarke <sofia.clarke@midlandbank.co.uk>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial compliance ask — SOC 2 Type II, DPA and interim coverage

Hi Sofia — quick technical follow-up from security engineering: 

1) Evidence we can provide immediately: 
   - PDF copy of the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
   - Interim coverage letter signed by our Compliance Director specifying control coverage and the audit window we are transitioning to
   - KMS configuration summary (attached) with redacted examples of CloudTrail logs showing key usage and rotation events

2) For additional depth (available on request): 
   - Redacted system access logs for deprovisioning controls (evidence for CC6/CC7 style controls)
   - A short runbook for our HSM/BYOK onboarding flow and expected timelines

3) Regarding region-specific controls: if Midland requires that both data plane and control plane be UK-only, we can provide either (a) a Private deployment package (dedicated VPC and control-plane placement) or (b) a legal attestation plus additional contractual DPA terms combined with technical mitigations (IP allowlisting, dedicated tenancy). Private deployments have a multi-week provisioning lead time and are typically part of Dedicated/Private agreements.

Please tell us which evidence set you want first (SOC2 + interim letter + KMS logs) and whether you require the control plane to be within the UK. We will prioritize accordingly.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Sofia Clarke <sofia.clarke@midlandbank.co.uk>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Procurement <legal@midlandbank.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial compliance ask — SOC 2 Type II, DPA and interim coverage

Marissa — thanks, that is helpful.

Procurement target: contract effective date 2026-04-01, so we need coverage from that date. Please proceed with an interim coverage letter scoped to 2026-04-01 through the anticipated audit completion (we understand the auditor timeline you mentioned).

For now the bank is OK with the control plane in eu-west-1 provided production workloads remain in eu-west-2 (London). We will flag a separate security requirement if we insist on a UK-only control plane.

Evidence request (priority order):
1) Interim coverage letter scoped to 2026-04-01
2) SOC 2 PDF (redacted ok)
3) KMS configuration summary + redacted CloudTrail key usage log sample
4) DPA draft (we will share comments once our legal team reviews)

If you can get the interim letter and SOC 2 by end of week, procurement will move to the legal review phase. Once we have the KMS artifacts we'll confirm the BYOK/HSM decision.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sofia
